text:
Renee (CS): Heads-up — Vetrix onboarding showing p95 tail jumps on /v1/chat (baseline p95 ~640ms -> ~1250ms last 48h). Renewal sync in 5 days. Thinking a conservative perf hedge: route short clinician replies to compact-mistral-6B-int8 and keep gpu-13B for long-context generation. want a short canary + offline QA (vetrix_clinical_suite).

Owen (Solutions): can you share p50/p95 and average token size? want a quick cost vs. quality calc.

Renee (CS): p50 300ms, p95 1250ms, avg payload ~130 tokens (but some 400+). sample prompt: "Summarize today's patient visit and list immediate follow-ups for meds and labs." Historically compact-mistral kept entity fidelity but phrasing differed.

Jules (SRE): any correlation w/ KV cache misses or batch imports?

Renee (CS): spikes line up with nightly ETL at 02:10 UTC and preview bursts midday — likely cache churn. routing by size should smooth the tail.

Owen (Solutions): proposed plan: 1) run offline eval on vetrix_clinical_suite (metrics: entity-F1, ROUGE, hallucination rate); 2) routing rule: prefer compact-mistral-6B-int8 when request.tokens <= 700; 3) canary 12% for 12h; 4) auto-rollback if UI feedback rate >1.2% in 30m or automated hallucination >0.8%.

Maya (Customer): clinicians need a feedback toggle with a short reason dropdown (missing follow-up / wrong med / unclear). we want flagged examples sent to our QA channel. if quality regresses, auto-rollback please.

Jules (SRE): will stand up canary and add rollback hooks. thresholds: feedback_thresh=0.012, eval_window=30m. also will temporarily limit ETL concurrency during the test window.

Owen (Solutions): Redwood Console routing snippet (pseudo-yaml):
```yaml
rules:
  - name: mistral-compact-pref
    match: route.path == "/v1/chat" and request.tokens <= 700
    prefer: compact-mistral-6B-int8
    fallback: gpu-13B
    canary_percent: 12
    window: 12h
    auto_rollback_on_feedback: true
```

Renee (CS): assigning: @Owen run offline eval & A/B diffs, @Jules run canary infra + rollback, @Maya enable feedback toggle and QA forward. I'll add a short remediation note to the renewal packet.

canary-bot: Canary created (id: canary-8734567890). Observability: https://console.redwood/example/canary/canary-8734567890

Jules (SRE): canary live. initial metrics: canary p95=500ms, baseline p95=1220ms. quick sample QA (n=25) shows 5 phrasing diffs, 0 entity errors. feedback widget enabled.

Owen (Solutions): early numbers: routed p95 down ~59% for short requests, estimated token-cost reduction ~42% on routed traffic. if offline eval entity-F1 delta <1.5% and hallucination <0.8% we recommend ramp to 50% over 24h.

Maya (Customer): feedback toggle live. clinicians flagged 2 outputs (style); both sent to our QA channel with short notes. please notify if anything escalates.

Jules (SRE): auto-rollback not triggered. feedback rate 0.7% after 4h. streaming alerts to #cs-renewals and to Maya's QA channel.

Owen (Solutions): eval finished: entity-F1 delta -0.9%, ROUGE drop 1.1, automated hallucination 0.4%. artifacts uploaded to renewal folder. drafting a one-slide summary for renewal call.

Renee (CS): renewal brief note: "Proactive perf mitigation executed: compact-mistral-6B-int8 canary reduced p95 for routed short traffic by ~59% with projected token-cost savings ~42%; quality within guardrails. recommend ramp plan in packet." Will include flagged examples in the deck and update after the ramp window. :white_check_mark:
